items.title: Is AI absorbing capital that used to go to crypto?
points: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs (funds holding actual bitcoin that trade on stock exchanges) saw $5.4B in net outflows in H1 2026 as money rotated into AI-linked assets.
Global equities — S&P 500, Dow, MSCI All Country World Index — hit record highs while Bitcoin stalled around $64,000, boxed in the $62,000–$65,000 range since May.
DWF Labs: 'Institutional and retail interest in crypto as an investment has cooled as AI absorbs a disproportionate share of capital and attention.'
Tether's $4B market cap contraction over 60 days hints at late-stage crypto selling, though no recovery signal has confirmed.

items.title: Coldcard hack sends bitcoin network activity to multi-month highs
points: A $120M hack of Coldcard hardware wallets pushed holders to move coins to fresh wallets and exchanges.
Unconfirmed transactions in the mempool (queue of pending bitcoin transactions) reached 89,031 — the highest since February 2025.
Active addresses climbed to a three-month high of 712,000; whale transactions (very large investor transfers) hit a five-month high of 61,800.
Rising network activity is usually constructive for price, yet Bitcoin's range has not broken.

items.title: Arthur Hayes: AI is a 2008-style credit bubble, not dot-com
points: Hayes argues hyperscalers are borrowing against data centers full of depreciating chips, echoing 2007 mortgage lending against depreciating real estate — a credit-driven, not earnings-driven, bubble.
Credit keeps flowing past the point capex (capital expenditure, i.e. spending on physical assets) stops accelerating; Hayes pegs that inflection at late 2027 into 2028.
A government bailout via money printing, justified on national-security grounds, would flood liquidity and push Bitcoin toward $1 million after a bottom.

items.title: The 10-year real yield is the key macro tripwire
points: The 10-year real yield (inflation-adjusted return on U.S. government bonds) sits at 2.41%, nine basis points (0.09 percentage points) below the 2.5% level above which Bitcoin has no historical price data.
If the yield clears and holds above 2.5%, the macro tailwind supporting Bitcoin valuations disappears entirely.

items.title: Solana is about to burn a lot more SOL every day
points: A completed network upgrade raises Solana's daily SOL burn rate, permanently removing more tokens from circulation each day.
Burning means sending tokens to an address no one can spend from, cutting total supply and increasing scarcity for remaining coins.
The change reshapes Solana's tokenomics (rules governing how many tokens exist and how they circulate) toward long-term deflationary pressure.
Burn volume scales with network activity, so heavy transaction periods create a self-reinforcing scarcity loop.

Near-term price impact depends on whether markets already priced the change in; Solana is competing with Ethereum and Avalanche on Layer 1 (base blockchains that settle transactions themselves) economics.

items.title: Indian Gaming Association pushes to bar prediction markets from Clarity Act
points: IGA VP Tehassi Hill urged the Senate to amend the Clarity Act to ban sports and casino gambling via prediction markets (venues where users bet on real-world outcomes) and affirm state/tribal jurisdiction over the CFTC.
CFTC Chair Michael Selig claims exclusive federal jurisdiction and has sued multiple states; Polymarket and Kalshi prefer CFTC oversight.
Senator Tina Smith floated adding similar language to the Farm Bill; Senate Agriculture Chair John Boozman called it separate from crypto, blocking Clarity inclusion.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation proposal would burn validator rewards to cap staking at 50%
points: Justin Drake co-authored an EIP for tapered issuance burn — destroying a rising share of validator rewards (payments to those locking ETH to secure the network) as the staking ratio climbs — hitting 100% burn at ~60.25M ETH staked, about 50% of supply.
Currently ~32M ETH (26% of supply) is staked; the mechanism phases in over 18 months to avoid concentration among large custodians, submitted ahead of the Hegotá upgrade deadline.
Aave's Stani Kulechov warns it would kill ETH borrowing and DeFi yield products; Grayscale's Zach Pandl says lower inflation is bullish for ETH.

items.title: BlackRock's Ethereum ETF plans a 3-for-1 reverse split
points: The October reverse split (combining shares to raise per-share price) is expected to cut trading spreads from 7 basis points (0.07% cost per trade) to 2 basis points.

items.title: Western Union Stablecard goes live via Rain
points: Remittances can now arrive as stablecoins (tokens pegged to a currency like the dollar) spendable directly at Visa merchants worldwide.

items.title: The wallet endgame is 'open money'
points: Self-custody wallets hold 'open money' moved directly on public blockchains, versus 'closed money' that is merely a claim on an institution's ledger.
MetaMask's mUSD stablecoin earns up to 6% APY via onchain lending with no lockup; the MetaMask Card keeps assets self-custodied until the moment of merchant payment.
ERC-7710 (delegation) and ERC-7715 (permission requests) let users grant scoped authority to AI agents, while x402 extends this to per-request machine-to-machine HTTP payments.
Wallets are becoming the 'permission layer' where delegated agents move money inside user-defined limits.

items.title: Bitcoin's quantum threat: real but slow-moving
points: Shor's algorithm could break Bitcoin's ECDSA/Schnorr signatures; Grover's algorithm against SHA-256 mining would need ~3% of the Sun's energy output, making the mining threat negligible.
About 6.26M BTC has exposed public keys: 1.7M BTC in legacy P2PK outputs is immediately vulnerable, and 5.2M BTC in reused or Taproot addresses needs migration.

Estimates for a cryptographically capable quantum computer span 10–40 years; BIP-360, adding Dilithium post-quantum signatures (math immune to quantum attacks) under a bc1z address type, was merged in early 2026 with a 7-year deployment window.
Classical (non-quantum) cryptanalysis is the stronger near-term reason to upgrade.

items.title: Who actually banks the stablecoin neobanks
points: Across five tested neobanks, EUR-to-stablecoin round trips on €5,000 cost $2–$130; RedotPay charged ~2% with ~60-hour clearing, while Avici had near-zero fees but week-long invasive KYC (identity verification).
USD rails are cheaper and more uniform at $2–$16 round-trip via ACH.
Bridge, Due, Noah, OpenPayd and Monerium are the main infrastructure vendors behind these apps; costs are driven by compliance friction, forex spreads and banking partner architecture.

items.title: Base ecosystem growth
points: Base, a layer-2 blockchain (a faster network settling onto Ethereum), captured 90% of agentic stablecoin transaction volume in Q2 2026 and tripled its onchain spot volume share over the past year.
B20s (Base Native Token Standard) hit $200M volume in 30 days on mainnet; Bankr platform coins passed $5B cumulative volume; Morpho's market crossed $500M with no token incentives.
Axis Robotics raised $12M seed for a Physical AI data engine on Base; Exa App raised $2.2M for onchain self-custody credit; MoonPay launched conversational AI trading for Claude/ChatGPT users.
Coinbase's borrow product hit all-time highs as the largest DeFi 'mullet' (crypto rails on the backend, familiar banking interface on the front).

items.title: Minor updates
points: DeFi Kingdoms is shutting down its proprietary DFKChain Layer-1 on August 28.
Visa's Q3 FY26 earnings call endorsed the OpenUSD stablecoin, citing neutral governance and shared economics.
Tornado Cash logged 968 deposits on July 23, its busiest day of 2026, moving 29,573 ETH ($57.2M) across 110 addresses.

issues.subject: Solana Is About to Burn a Lot More SOL Every Day

headlines: Solana will burn significantly more SOL tokens daily after a network upgrade, reducing token supply and potentially supporting price appreciation.
Token burn mechanisms remove coins from circulation permanently, decreasing total supply and increasing scarcity value for remaining tokens.
The increased burn rate follows Solana's push to improve network economics and make SOL more deflationary.
Higher SOL burns could benefit long-term holders by making the asset scarcer, though near-term price impacts depend on network usage patterns.
Solana developers implemented the upgrade to enhance the blockchain's economic model amid growing competition from other Layer 1 networks.

sections.title: Solana's Token Burn Upgrade
points: 1. Solana network completed an upgrade increasing the daily SOL burn rate, meaning more tokens are permanently removed from circulation each day.
2. Burn mechanisms work by sending tokens to non-recoverable addresses; this permanently reduces the total supply available in the market.
3. The change targets Solana's tokenomics (the rules governing how many tokens exist and how they're distributed) to create long-term deflationary pressure.
4. Developers designed this upgrade to differentiate Solana's economic model from competitors and incentivize holding rather than selling.

sections.title: Implications for SOL Holders and Network
points: 1. Increased scarcity could benefit existing SOL holders if demand remains stable or grows, as fewer tokens chase the same value.
2. The burn rate increase ties directly to network activity—more transactions generate more burn, creating a virtuous cycle during periods of high usage.
3. Short-term price effects depend on whether the market has already priced in the burn increase; if unexpected, it could spark buying interest.
4. Solana competes with Ethereum, Avalanche, and other Layer 1 blockchains (networks that process transactions independently) for developer and user adoption.
